channel.title: c4573.org — Blog
channel.description: Essays on technofeudalism, acceleration, and owning your tools.

item.title: d/acc Has a Build Order
item.description: Four camps argue about how fast while the intelligence layer gets built as rental property. Only one framework answers what to build first. Where d/acc came from, what actually backs it, and the strongest case against it.

item.title: Chicken Little Goes to Washington
item.description: Eliezer Yudkowsky spent years insisting that artificial intelligence would kill everyone. Bernie Sanders has now turned the fable into a federal agency, a permanent global ban, corporate dissolution, and twenty years in prison.

item.title: Research property near SpaceX’s Starbase with Texas public records
item.description: A runnable Python example, dated CSV/JSON output, and a narrated Cameron County property demo. No account or dependencies.

item.title: The Right Argument, the Wrong Messenger
item.description: Zuckerberg wrote the strongest open-source argument a frontier CEO has ever put on paper. It is an argument against its own author. Concentration is the risk — which is exactly why "trust me, I'll distribute it" is the danger wearing a friendly face.

item.title: Schmidt Was Right
item.description: Eric Schmidt got booed for fifteen minutes at a commencement. The argument under the rocket ship line was correct. The boos mechanically produce the worst version of the transition.

item.title: The Moratorium Is a Concession Speech
item.description: Sanders and AOC want to pause data center construction until Congress figures out AI. The intent is good. The game theory is fatal.

item.title: Software Was Never the Endpoint
item.description: Intelligence is getting cheaper. The next step is applying it where scarcity still lives: the physical world. The only real question is who owns it when it gets there.

item.title: The Exposure Gap
item.description: AI is theoretically capable of replacing 94% of tasks in Computer & Math jobs. It is covering 33% today. That gap is not reassurance — it is a timeline.

item.title: The Severance Protocol
item.description: Six hundred and forty-two thousand tech workers laid off in a single year. One in four were explicitly told to "AI-driven restructuring." This is the protocol that replaces them.

item.title: The Helicopter and the Hike
item.description: Terence Tao says AI is doing math now. Here's what he actually said, and why the tech press got it wrong.

item.title: Ghost GDP and the People Who Become the Ghosts
item.description: A credible crisis scenario, translated from investor-speak into what it actually means.

item.title: The Elysium Thesis Is Right About the Problem and Wrong About the Endpoint
item.description: On AI, power concentration, 20-watt brains, and why science always wins.

item.title: You Can't Ban Math: AI, Data Centers, and the Fear Response
item.description: Fear leads to bans. Bans lead to irrelevance. Reality requires building.

item.title: Texas Scraper Kit: 10 Verified Scrapers, 261 Beta Modules, $13.37.
item.description: Announcing the Texas Scraper Kit — the first tool from c4573.org. Who it's for, what it does, and why it costs less than lunch.

item.title: Three Companies Control Commoditized Intelligence. Now What?
item.description: On technofeudalism, escape velocity, and why the only way out is through.
